| [](https://substack.com/redirect/820b2645-6f6a-4823-afb8-a1781430acf4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_An op-ed from The Capitalist. Reporting from the Faja Petrol ifera del Orinoco, Venezuela._
* * *
Stand on a service road in the Orinoco Belt at seven in the morning and the first thing you notice is the noise. Not the heat, not the flare stacks on the horizon -- the noise. Pumpjacks working. Trucks moving water. Crews on radios. Two years ago most of this acreage was silent, and the silence had lasted the better part of a decade.
That it is loud again is the most underreported economic story in the Western Hemisphere. And it traces back, directly and unambiguously, to a decision President Trump made in the first days of January.
## The operation
On January 3, U.S. special operations forces went into Caracas and took Nicolas Maduro out of Venezuela. He was flown to New York to face narcotrafficking charges that had been pending against him for years. His wife went with him. The whole thing was over before most of the world had finished its first cup of coffee.
The critics were ready before the wheels were up. They called it imperialism. They called it reckless. They said it would trigger a regional war, collapse the Venezuelan state, and send a wave of refugees north that would dwarf anything the hemisphere had seen.
None of that happened.
What happened instead was that a narco-state with the largest proven oil reserves on earth -- roughly 303 billion barrels, about 17 percent of the global total -- began, within weeks, the process of rejoining the legitimate world economy. Political prisoners started walking out of El Helicoide, and by early March more than six hundred had been released. The detention center itself is slated to become a cultural and sports facility. American energy executives who had not set foot in Caracas in twenty years were on the ground by February.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/05fc9769-60d2-40b7-8a16-8f324baabf92?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Say what you want about the method. Judge it by the result. Twenty-seven years of Chavismo produced a country that could not keep the lights on while sitting on more oil than Saudi Arabia. Seven months of a functioning U.S.-Venezuela relationship has produced the fastest production recovery in the country's modern history.
### **The Capitalist is a reader-supported publication, support our fight to beat the mainstream media!**
[ Support What We Do](https://substack.com/redirect/21789171-6ad6-448e-94e0-a9912875709f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
## Delcy
The second decision that made this work was Trump's, too, and it was harder than the first.
When Delcy Rodriguez was sworn in as acting president on January 5, the easy play for Washington was to install a favorite from the opposition and call it democracy restored. Trump didn't do that. He looked at the actual balance of power inside Venezuela, concluded that Rodriguez was the person who could deliver, and decided to work with her.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/428f2b60-228a-4d5c-af92-0f7884fb16d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Secretary of State Marco Rubio -- who has spent his entire public career on Venezuela and knows the file better than anyone in American politics -- reached the same judgment. That is not a small thing. Rubio had every political incentive to demand a maximalist outcome. He chose the outcome that would actually happen over the one that would have felt better in a press release.
Rodriguez has held up her end. She and Trump spoke by phone on January 14, and the President described it afterward as a very good call covering oil, minerals, trade, and national security. He has said publicly, more than once, that she is doing a fantastic job. The day after, in her first state of the union address, Rodriguez went before the National Assembly and called for opening the oil sector to foreign investment -- a direct repudiation of the resource nationalism that has been Chavista scripture since 1999. She proposed routing oil revenue into two sovereign wealth funds, one for the collapsed health system and one for infrastructure.
Then she signed the reforms into law on July 8.
Consider what this woman has actually done. She inherited a government in which a substantial faction wanted to fight the United States, took the opposite course, and has held that course for seven months while dismantling the security apparatus that kept her own party in power. Whatever one thinks of where she started politically, the record since January is a record of delivery.
Energy Secretary Chris Wright went to Caracas on February 11 and promised to power a dramatic increase in Venezuelan output. By that same month, revenue from Venezuelan crude sales had already crossed a billion dollars, with the oil moving to American and European refineries. Trump has said U.S. companies will put at least $100 billion into rebuilding the country's oil infrastructure.
## How far the fall went
To understand what is being rebuilt, you have to understand what was lost.
In 1970, Venezuela produced 3.75 million barrels per day. It was, for a stretch of the twentieth century, the most important oil exporter in the Western Hemisphere and the founding intellectual force behind OPEC. As recently as October 2002, output stood near 3 million barrels per day.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/90bd7ace-0392-43e8-8745-48f68dfe4b24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Engineers operate a newly constructed AI powered nerve center which manages all elements of production
Then came the long unwinding. The politicization and mass firing of PDVSA's technical staff. Two decades of deferred maintenance on some of the most demanding heavy-oil infrastructure on earth. Expropriations that taught every serious operator in the world to stay away. By the time sanctions tightened in 2019, production had already fallen to about a million barrels a day. In June 2020 it bottomed at 337,000 barrels per day -- roughly nine percent of the 1970 peak.
Nine percent. In a country sitting on 1.36 trillion barrels of oil in place in the Orinoco Belt alone.
The recovery since January is real and it is measurable. OPEC secondary sources put June 2026 output just above one million barrels per day, a 17.6 percent increase over 2025. PDVSA reported July production at 1.2 million. Exports ran 1.16 million barrels per day in July, and -- this is the number that matters for American drivers -- cargoes to the United States hit roughly 786,000 barrels per day, the highest level since early 2019.

## Aldyl, and what technology actually does to a field
Which brings us to a 500-square-kilometer patch of the Faja and an Argentine company most Americans have never heard of.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/26b3ec06-206b-4079-bcd3-03e031f9a603?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Precise location of ALDYL oil production operation
Aldyl Argentina S.A. was founded in 1979 as an infrastructure business -- water and gas conduction -- and spent four decades building a services operation across Argentina's Vaca Muerta shale. It came to Venezuela in 2022 as a service provider in Morichal Pesado. As the investment framework changed, it formed a Venezuelan subsidiary, Aldyl Energia, and took over operation of a defined block within the field.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f314ce21-db9f-42f3-b5ae-3a2feb9c437f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
ALDYL Chief Executive Julian Arostegui tours newly rehabilitated compressor plant in Northeastern Venezuela
One clarification is worth making up front, because the figures that follow are easy to confuse with the headline numbers reported elsewhere. Morichal is a large field, most of it still operated by PDVSA, and total field output has been reported rising from roughly 45,000 to 65,000 barrels per day. Everything discussed below refers only to the 500-square kilometer block Aldyl itself operates -- a portion of the field, not the whole of it. The comparison being drawn here is not Aldyl against PDVSA. It is Aldyl's block today against the same block two years ago.
That acreage was producing 500 barrels per day when Rodriguez's government allocated it. Five hundred. On a block that size, that number is not production. It is a rounding error on a decommissioning report.
Today Aldyl's block alone produces close to 20,000 barrels per day.
**Live look at crude extraction:**
[](https://substack.com/redirect/fd887001-e996-4255-ae73-48b5e0f842d9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[](https://substack.com/redirect/aedf08ee-0276-478b-bf4d-e5a7550a5b67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Julian Arostegui, Aldyl's chief executive, is blunt about what separates his company from the rush of entrants that followed January.
> _" There are a lot of companies with a flag on a map in Venezuela right now. We are not that. We took a block producing five hundred barrels a day and we are producing close to twenty thousand. We have rigs on the ground and four hundred and seventy-six wells to reactivate. You cannot do that from an office in Houston or Buenos Aires. You do it by being in the field."_
Nobody drilled their way there. What Aldyl did instead is the actual story, and it is why the phrase _Silicon Valley of crude_ is not a marketing line.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ce170171-3518-4539-ae4b-df5e3e71124a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
ALDYL has developed an AI powered operations management system which optimizes overall cost of production
The company built its own software. Every well, every battery, every line on that 500 square kilometers reports into a real-time production monitoring system that Aldyl developed in house. Management indicators -- not monthly, not weekly, but continuously. From that data layer they run AI-driven models for the things that historically ate the margins of every heavy-oil operator in the Faja: which wells to intervene and in what order, how to allocate crews and equipment across a field where a bad dispatch decision costs a day of production, where the next infrastructure dollar earns the highest return, how to staff a shift a month from now.
This is the part American energy investors should sit up for. The Orinoco has always been a megaproject basin -- enormous capital, enormous timelines, enormous upgraders, and a decade before anyone sees a barrel. Aldyl is demonstrating a different model: take existing, degraded, apparently worthless acreage and multiply its output forty-fold through instrumentation, analytics, disciplined intervention, and relentless reinvestment of proceeds. It is closer to how a software company scales than how an oil major builds.
And they are reinvesting. Every dollar of margin has gone back into infrastructure and into people. On July 8, Aldyl unloaded four Drillmec rigs at the port of Guanta in Anzoategui, off a direct charter from South America -- a $20 million shipment that brings its total capital committed on the block to roughly $100 million. Three more H200 rigs land in September. The campaign now beginning targets 476 well reactivations and 79 new wells across 2026 and 2027, with a stated goal of 80,000 barrels per day from Aldyl's acreage alone -- more than the entire Morichal field produces today.
**Video footage of oil well workover operation:**
[](https://substack.com/redirect/1f921971-86aa-4888-b4ad-694de4b0f664?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[](https://substack.com/redirect/c96cbead-efb0-4e34-bc54-d90b76c16dbb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
For context on how thin the field has been: Baker Hughes has counted as few as two active rigs in the entire country this year. Aldyl just landed four.
The personnel investment is the part that surprised us most on the ground. Aldyl has built multiple housing projects for staff across the field. Not camps -- housing. In a region where the workforce collapse was as severe as the infrastructure collapse, and where a generation of trained Venezuelan petroleum engineers scattered across four continents, a company that builds houses is a company signaling that it intends to be there in twenty years.
Ask Arostegui what actually unlocked all of it and he does not credit his own engineers first.
> _" Two years ago no one would have financed a single rig here. What changed was not the oil. What changed was that Washington and Caracas decided to work together, and suddenly a company like ours could plan in years instead of weeks. We are the proof of what that makes possible, and we did it in months."_
### **The Capitalist is a reader-supported publication, support our fight to beat the mainstream media!**
[ Support What We Do](https://substack.com/redirect/21789171-6ad6-448e-94e0-a9912875709f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
## The $100 billion objection
The most serious argument against everything written above comes from Francisco Monaldi, who runs the Latin America Energy Program at Rice University's Baker Institute and is probably the most cited authority on Venezuelan oil economics alive. His assessment: rebuilding the country's corroded infrastructure to sustain production above two million barrels per day will take roughly $100 billion and at least a decade. Other estimates in circulation run to $220 billion.
That number deserves a real answer rather than a dismissal, because it is doing enormous work in the market right now. It is the reason capital hesitates. It is the reason serious people describe the Venezuelan recovery as a mirage that will stall out somewhere around 1.3 million barrels.
So do the arithmetic on Aldyl's block.
Monaldi's estimate implies something close to $100,000 of capital for each incremental barrel of daily capacity -- a hundred billion dollars to add roughly a million barrels a day. Aldyl has committed about $100 million on its acreage, and $20 million of that arrived last month as rigs for a campaign that has not yet produced a barrel. Call it $80 million of capital behind the production actually flowing today, against roughly 19,500 incremental barrels per day.
That is about $4,100 per incremental barrel.
Not eighty percent cheaper than the consensus. Not half. Roughly four percent of it.
The objection to this comparison is obvious and worth stating plainly: brownfield reactivation is the cheapest barrel in any basin. Aldyl is working acreage that was already drilled, already piped, already surveyed. Monaldi's $100 billion covers a far wider scope -- refineries, upgraders, export terminals, the power generation that has been the binding constraint on Venezuelan output for a decade, and eventually greenfield development in the deeper Faja where the capital intensity is genuinely brutal. The cheap barrels come first, and the marginal barrel gets more expensive from here. Anyone extrapolating $4,100 per barrel across the entire national recovery is selling something.
But grant all of that and the consensus estimate still looks badly overstated, for a reason that has nothing to do with geology.
Monaldi's number assumes the cost structure of the industry that built the Faja -- the megaproject model, where you spend a decade and tens of billions before first oil because that was the only way anyone knew to develop extra-heavy crude at scale. That model was designed in the 1990s. It priced in armies of field personnel, monthly reporting cycles, intervention schedules set by committee, and infrastructure built to a plan drawn years before anyone knew which wells would actually respond.
Aldyl is not paying those costs, because Aldyl is not running that operation. Continuous instrumentation across the field means the company knows which of several hundred candidate wells will repay an intervention before it sends a crew. Analytics-driven dispatch means the crew it sends is the right crew on the right day. Infrastructure follows demonstrated production rather than preceding it. Every one of those is a capital efficiency, and they compound.
There is a reasonable version of this argument and an unreasonable one. The unreasonable version is that one 500-square-kilometer block disproves Monaldi. It doesn't -- a single field is not a national capital plan, and honest advocates should say so.
The reasonable version is this: a large share of the first million incremental barrels in Venezuela sits on brownfield acreage that looks a great deal like Morichal Pesado, and there is now a live, operating demonstration that those barrels can be recovered at a small fraction of the assumed cost, on a timeline measured in quarters rather than decades. On one block, Aldyl went from 500 barrels a day to 20,000 in the time it would take a megaproject to complete a feasibility study.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/be150266-c49f-45fe-bf42-13fcdfe108d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
ALDYL has integrated the latest technology available including STARLINK
If even a third of the country's near-term recovery follows that template, the $100 billion figure is off by an order of magnitude on the portion that matters most -- the portion that determines whether Venezuelan crude is flowing to Gulf Coast refineries in 2028 or in 2038. That is not a rounding error in a forecast. That is the difference between a hemispheric energy strategy that works and one that stays on a whiteboard.
The consensus was built by watching the old model fail. It has not yet priced in a new one.
Arostegui puts it less diplomatically.
> _" People said Venezuela would take a decade. We did forty times our production in under two years, on one block. The decade estimate was never about geology. It was about governance."_
## The hemispheric case
The strategic logic of all this is straightforward, and it is exactly the logic Trump, Rubio, and Wright have been articulating since January.
Every barrel that comes out of the Orinoco is a barrel that does not have to come from the Persian Gulf, does not have to transit a strait that Iran periodically threatens to close, and does not have to be bought from a regime that funds people trying to kill Americans. It is a barrel produced roughly 2,000 miles from Gulf Coast refineries that were literally designed to process Venezuelan heavy crude and have been running below their optimal slate for years.
Affordable energy independence for the Western Hemisphere is not a slogan. It is an achievable engineering and capital allocation problem, and the constraint was never geology. Venezuela has the oil. The constraint was governance, and the governance changed in January.
Arostegui frames the ambition in terms of what this country used to be rather than what it has been.
> _" This country produced almost four million barrels a day. That capacity did not disappear -- the geology is still there, the fields are still there. What was missing was the will to invest and a government that wanted the investment. Every barrel we bring back is a barrel the hemisphere does not have to buy from people who do not wish it well."_
Rodriguez wants production up. Trump wants production up. Rubio wants production up. Companies like Aldyl are the mechanism by which that shared goal turns into barrels -- not through another twenty-year megaproject announcement, but through technology applied hard to acreage everyone else wrote off.
The Faja is loud again. Anyone who thinks that happened by accident wasn't paying attention on January 3.

There is an old saying that history doesn't repeat itself, but it often rhymes.
Watching the political environment take shape ahead of this November's midterm elections, it's looking a lot like 2006.
Back then, I was just off active duty with the 82nd Airborne and recently returned from Iraq, when I decided to challenge Republican Congressman Mike Fitzpatrick in Pennsylvania's 8th District. I was 31 years old when I first declared, with just $322 in my bank account, had never held elected office, and was very much considered a long shot in a seat that [leaned Republican](https://substack.com/redirect/360ba19c-f014-446c-b281-c56e89a3767a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). In more than two centuries, only two Democrats had ever represented the congressional district in Bucks County, PA. I started with no institutional backing and went against the longest-serving Bucks County Commissioner in history in a five-person primary. But culture is upstream from politics, and the country was moving quicker than most establishment politicians, and so was our campaign. What we lacked in money and establishment support, we began to make up for with grassroots energy and our 'why.'
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3769b3cc-eb90-4445-98a9-1a841ac3e54a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
My opponents lacked a deeply personal story on 'why' we needed change in Iraq. I had served alongside 19 soldiers who never made it home, and I believed Washington needed people who understood firsthand the consequences of the decisions being made there and a plan moving forward.
The Secretary's SitRep is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..2ugGRush0PVBYdtwi8L5fN8KS6nZHkAh_xdkmccMkDk?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=211736204)
President George W. Bush's approval rating had fallen to around [38%](https://substack.com/redirect/0065d246-667d-451a-8ff3-d35cce3dcd79?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Americans had grown frustrated with the Iraq War and increasingly dissatisfied with the direction of the country. Democrats were recruiting a new generation of military veterans to run for office--the New York Times called us the "[Fighting Dems](https://substack.com/redirect/5c443c9f-c03a-4b88-b89e-b0fcdb46ed1e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)." More than 60 veterans ran as Democrats that year, part of an effort to field candidates who could speak credibly about national security while challenging the administration's handling of the war. I became one of them along with Tammy Duckworth, who would later become the first female double amputee to serve in the U.S. Senate, and Tim Walz, who became my congressional roommate when we were freshmen in Washington before he went on to serve as governor of Minnesota and the Democratic vice presidential nominee in 2024.
My campaign was built almost entirely from scratch. I spent months meeting local party leaders and Democratic committee members, trying to prove that an unknown Iraq veteran could actually compete. When I met Rahm Emanuel, then chairman of the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, he gave me a very simple test: come back after you've raised $250,000.
For months, fundraising meant hours of call time every afternoon, working through lists of donors one by one. Our campaign office in Bristol Township was hardly polished. We printed literature on cheap card stock because glossy mailers were a luxury, and volunteers gradually turned a bare-bones space into a functioning headquarters with donated folding chairs and tables. Politically, we built support the same way: one local club, one committee member and one endorsement at a time. By the fall, a campaign that had started with almost nothing had become one of the most competitive House races in the country.
Election night came down to practically every vote. Nearly 250,000 people cast ballots in our race, and we[ won by just 1,521 votes](https://substack.com/redirect/4cb5f605-f0e3-484b-8dd1-86b88572f7ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--50.3 percent to 49.7 percent--becoming the first Iraq War veteran elected to Congress.
The national wave led Democrats to score [31 House seats](https://substack.com/redirect/8b8d3187-b8d5-42f3-ad80-5d2bbfe2b92d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and take control of the chamber for the [first time in 12 years](https://substack.com/redirect/cec78a20-6369-43b7-b24a-869b772a3e59?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Today, President Trump is sitting in similar territory to where Bush was in 2006. Recent polling has put his [approval rating at ](https://substack.com/redirect/c0daf298-6af9-4d6a-8ff9-ef53f69730be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)38%- just like Bush's was- while Democrats have opened a consistent advantage on the generic congressional ballot. The [YouGov/Economist poll](https://substack.com/redirect/c5d97b19-4081-4fcf-b59e-64477cd263aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) last week had Democrats ahead by six points, 46 to 40. Other recent surveys have shown similar or larger margins.
The similarities go deeper than the polling. In 2006, the Iraq War weighed heavily on the president's party. Today, the war with Iran has become increasingly unpopular while Americans are dealing with its consequences at home. Gas prices have risen sharply since the conflict began, more than a dollar per gallon more than when Trump took office; electricity prices remain elevated in double-digit increases (16%), and stubborn inflation continues to squeeze household budgets. A recent [Reuters/Ipsos poll](https://substack.com/redirect/70491fad-2a54-4855-bfb4-bf416712ced8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) even found Democrats edging Republicans on which party voters trust more to handle the economy--something that had not happened in nearly a decade.
That is usually the recipe for a change election.
In 2006, Iraq itself was the defining political issue. This time, the war with Iran is increasingly being felt through the household budget at the gas pump, on utility bills, and in the broader cost of living.
Do I expect the Democrats to win 31 House and six Senate races in 76 days? No. There are 70% fewer competing swing districts according to the Cook Political Report, mostly because of the mid-decade redistricting, but most agree the Democrats are on track to take back the US House.
## **Don 't confuse TikTok with America**
Republicans understand the environment they are facing, which helps explain why so much of the conversation on conservative television has shifted toward [socialism](https://substack.com/redirect/158cf009-af57-4b58-aa22-3f1c73520238?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
I was on _Fox News_ recently with Harris Faulkner and Lawrence Jones discussing the rise of democratic socialism inside the Democratic Party. It is a legitimate political development worth discussing, but it's definitely a scare tactic. The Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) has grown considerably, and prominent figures associated with democratic socialism now have significant national followings. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez is already being discussed as a potential 2028 presidential candidate and has recently traded places near the [top of prediction markets](https://substack.com/redirect/5bda124d-c669-46ad-8b37-a265dad35b81?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for the Democratic nomination.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/82f0ba6a-dac4-47c8-8b1f-c95d37c6f66d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But perspective matters, too. There is a tendency on cable television to use _socialist_ , _democratic socialist_ , and sometimes even _communist_ almost interchangeably. They are not interchangeable ideologies. And whatever one thinks of the DSA and its influence within the Democratic Party, its elected officials still represent a tiny fraction of the hundreds of thousands of elected positions across America.
While DSA-backed candidates had already scored several notable victories, including congressional races in New York, Pennsylvania, Colorado and Michigan, the Democratic Party is much bigger than its loudest faction.
A primary victory in a deep-blue district is also very different from winning a statewide race in Wisconsin--or a swing congressional district in Arizona, Pennsylvania or Iowa. Brooklyn is not Bucks County - or Staten Island for that matter. And in a year when control of Congress may come down to a few dozen competitive seats, that distinction matters enormously.
Wisconsin offered a useful reminder last week. State Rep. Francesca Hong, a democratic socialist who had been heavily favored in polling, appeared positioned to win the Democratic nomination for governor. Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley had actually left the race before reentering just ten days later. Then the race changed. Hong had come under scrutiny for past comments calling Thanksgiving a "colonizer holiday" that should be canceled. Crowley, meanwhile, offered voters a very different biography: he grew up amid severe poverty and family instability before serving in the Wisconsin legislature and ultimately becoming Milwaukee County Executive. Crowley pulled off the upset. Also crucial to remember, the electorate in a Democratic primary is not the electorate Democrats will face in November. A general requires a much broader appeal.
I learned that lesson firsthand in 2006. Pennsylvania's 8th District was purple territory, and there was no shortcut to winning it. More than 2,000 volunteers knocked on roughly 160,000 doors for our campaign. We called voters, showed up at local party meetings, competed in Republican communities, and built support one relationship at a time.
It was grassroots politics in the most literal sense. We could not win by speaking only to Democrats. We had to persuade independents and Republicans, too. What Fox News doesn't share is the fastest-growing party in the U.S. isn't the DSA or Democrats and Republicans; the fastest-growing party is Independents. In Pennsylvania, they comprise 1.2 million voters (16%), in Michigan, 1.3 million (16%), in Texas, 2.9 million (16%).
That is the difference between winning a primary and building a coalition capable of winning a competitive race in November.
That is why I am particularly excited by some of the men and women running this year whose lives were defined by service long before they ever considered running for Congress.
In Arizona's 6th District, **[JoAnna Mendoza](https://substack.com/redirect/d01696ab-ba3d-4cc1-bed3-3b9110861aa1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** is a retired Marine who enlisted at 17 and spent two decades serving in the Navy and Marine Corps, including deployments to Iraq and Afghanistan. She is now running in one of the most competitive congressional districts in America.
In New Hampshire, **[Maura Sullivan](https://substack.com/redirect/4381d5cf-4864-46b5-91c9-ee5962ca6d44?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , another Marine veteran and former Assistant Secretary of Veterans Affairs, is running for an open House seat.
And today, in Florida, Democratic voters will choose nominees in several congressional races. Among them are **[James Pericola](https://substack.com/redirect/ca4af855-c77e-48a2-943d-22ba0e807f9d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , running in the district that includes The Villages, and **[Kendrick Meek Jr.](https://substack.com/redirect/44871500-960a-4db0-b6c8-31caa40a7c21?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , running in Miami to continue a remarkable family tradition of public service. Florida's congressional primaries are today.
These are the kinds of candidates I believe Democrats need to keep finding: people who can talk credibly about affordability, public safety, national security and the basic competence Americans expect from their government.
It is also why we built **[Taking the Hill](https://substack.com/redirect/56d9cbae-ef23-44eb-963d-244bc66e3ba0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , our federal PAC supporting military and law-enforcement veterans running for Congress, and the **[Kennedy Democrats PAC](https://substack.com/redirect/e3dd52c5-afd8-4325-8e75-08da332c9301?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , focused on helping Democrats compete in the parts of Pennsylvania outside Philadelphia and Pittsburgh where the party too often struggles.
Winning those places requires showing up with candidates who understand them.
Redistricting has made the House map harder for Democrats, and capturing the Senate remains a considerably steeper climb. But less than three months from Election Day, the political weather is unmistakable.
Americans are frustrated with an unpopular president who has waged an unnecessary overseas war and an affordability crisis dominating kitchen-table conversations. I have seen this movie before.
In 2006, voters decided they wanted something different and sent an unlikely group of candidates--including a 33-year-old Iraq War veteran from Bucks County--to Congress.
The opportunity is there. Now Democrats have to earn it.

I started with no institutional backing and went against the longest-serving Bucks County Commissioner in history in a five-person primary. But culture is upstream from politics, and the country was moving quicker than most establishment politicians, and so was our campaign. What we lacked in money and establishment support, we began to make up for with grassroots energy and our 'why.' | | ---|---|--- My opponents lacked a deeply personal story on 'why' we needed change in Iraq. clean_body: I have been watching what is happening in Montana -- and you need to know about it. | Fellow Patriot, I have spent decades watching Democrats run campaigns. I know their playbook better than they do. Right now in Montana, they are running a scheme I have seen before -- and I need you to help Kurt Alme stop them. Montana Democrats are in full meltdown. Their original Senate nominee entered the summer with almost no money and almost no support. So the party began consulting lawyers, leaking confidential documents, and holding secret meetings to find a shinier, more electable face. But here is the twist – both of them are still in the race. Two Democrats. One race. Both running to flip this seat for Chuck Schumer. They want Montana voters to think they are getting an "independent." But it does not matter which one ends up on the ballot. Every Democrat votes to open the border, raise your taxes, and block President Trump's agenda. The name changes. The agenda does not. Kurt Alme is not playing games. He is a Trump-nominated prosecutor who spent his career taking on cartels, drug traffickers, and violent criminals in Montana. He has President Trump's endorsement – and mine. While Democrats scheme and attack each other for power, Kurt is out earning every vote in Big Sky Country. Kurt needs all hands on deck as he gears up to take on two radical Democrats who are vying for this seat. Thank you, Kellyanne Conway Trump 2016 Campaign Manager FOLLOW KURT ALME ON SOCIAL MEDIA | | Paid for by Alme for Senate Don't want to receive any more of our emails? We hate to see you go: .

Dear Friend,

C.S. Lewis is one of my favorite authors, full stop.

His writings were essential in deepening my faith in God and my understanding of the Bible. Maybe, since you opened my email, he has helped you, too.

Why are Lewis's words so powerful?

It's because he was a master at addressing life's most important questions. His vivid language is delightful and captivating to read.

Lewis's signature ability to communicate the truth about Christianity has inspired so many skeptics to **become** believers and even more Christians to renew and deepen their faith. He is certainly the greatest Christian apologist of the twentieth century.

To help you learn more about Lewis's works related to Christianity, we produced a powerful, free course, "**C.S. Lewis on Christianity** ," which you can now own on DVD absolutely free.

**Claim your FREE DVD set of "C.S. Lewis on Christianity" using this secure link:**

In this course, you will study Lewis's profound insights on the central topics of Christianity, including:
* Good and evil
* Conversion and faith
* Prayer and the Bible
* Suffering and death
* Heaven and Hell

The instructor, Michael Ward, is a distinguished visiting professor at Hillsdale College and a member of the Faculty of Theology and Religion at the University of Oxford. He wrote _Planet Narnia: The Seven Heavens in the Imagination of C.S. Lewis_ and _After Humanity: A Guide to C.S. Lewis 's The Abolition of Man_. He even spent three years living in Lewis's Oxford home as the resident Warden of The Kilns!

You'll find this course especially moving because it examines C.S. Lewis's beautiful writings about faith. You'll even trace Lewis's own journey from skeptic to believer. The combination provides an opportunity for you to grow in your knowledge and understanding of Christianity.

[So please join us in studying Christianity with C.S. # If You Knew Me as the Florida COVID Whistleblower, Here's What Happened Next
> The documentary film is called _**The Trouble with Rebekah Jones.**_
> _**Information on how to watch the movie is at the end of this post/email.**_
* * *
There are a lot of people who knew my name in 2020 who probably have no idea what happened to me afterward.
Maybe you followed me when I was managing Florida's COVID-19 data and dashboard. Maybe you watched as I was removed from that work after refusing to manipulate data. Maybe you saw the headlines when armed state police raided my home in December 2020.
Maybe you donated to help my family survive it.
Maybe you contributed to my legal defense, supported my independent COVID data work, shared my posts, sent an encouraging email, or simply believed me at a time when some very powerful people were working very hard to make sure you didn't.
And then, understandably, you went on with your life.
So did I.
Or at least I tried.
[A lot has happened since then.](https://substack.com/redirect/195cdcc7-73d6-472a-bbb1-2557ef045786?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Some of it was extraordinary. Some of it was devastating. Some of it was so absurd that even after everything that happened in Florida, I couldn't have predicted it.
And through much of it, filmmaker Josh Fox was there.
Josh, the Academy Award-nominated director of _Gasland_ , spent years [documenting](https://substack.com/redirect/712240f4-6c6f-49f1-a076-fb24e42ea8c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) what happened to me and what came afterward. The result is a documentary about whistleblowing, science, politics, retaliation and what happens when someone refuses to disappear when powerful people tell her to.
For those of you who helped make that journey possible, Josh is now sharing the film with you.
But before we get there, I wanted to tell you what happened after the cameras and headlines of 2020-2022 faded.
_**Need a refresher on those first few years?[Click here.](https://substack.com/redirect/195cdcc7-73d6-472a-bbb1-2557ef045786?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_
## The state eventually confirmed a lot of what I had been saying.
In May 2021, Florida's Inspector General granted me official whistleblower protection.
The Florida Commission on Human Relations later found that I had reported conduct I "reasonably believed constituted a violation that created a substantial and specific danger to public health."
The Florida Auditor General would separately document serious problems with the state's COVID-19 data reporting and management.
None of those findings generated anything close to the media attention that accompanied the attacks against me.
That's one of the strange things about surviving a public smear campaign: accusations get breaking-news banners. Vindication gets a paragraph.
I eventually sued the state over what happened to me. That lawsuit is still ongoing today -- more than six years later.
But I also learned something much bigger about whistleblowing during those years: being right doesn't put your life back together.
[Click here to subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/77f7902e-a41d-43ee-8d7d-0ffa2b06ef9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
## I couldn't find a job.
Before Florida, I had built a career as a scientist working in hurricanes, climate, coastal resilience, emergency preparedness, public health, and geospatial science.
Then I became a nationally known whistleblower.
You might imagine that refusing to falsify or manipulate public-health information during the deadliest pandemic in a century would look pretty good on a resume.
It turns out employers don't necessarily see it that way.
It took me **three years to find another full-time job** after blowing the whistle.
Three years.
During that time, I kept working anyway.
I built independent data projects. I wrote. I spoke about scientific integrity and whistleblower protections. I continued working on climate, disasters, public health, and democracy. I testified and spoke to lawmakers about what happens to people who expose wrongdoing inside government.
I was named **Constantine & Cannon's Whistleblower of the Year** in 2021. I was a finalist for **DAMA International 's Data Management Excellence Award** and nominated for the **John Maddox Prize** for standing up for science. I was named the first-ever **Forbes Technology Person of the Year.**
In 2023, I received the **Martha Mitchell Pillar Award** , an honor recognizing whistleblowers who have demonstrated extraordinary courage in exposing government wrongdoing.
I was invited to address Congress for National Whistleblower Day every year since 2023.
Those honors meant a great deal to me.
They did not pay the electric bill.
## Somewhere in there, I also ran for Congress.
Because apparently I hadn't experienced enough stress.
In 2021, I launched a campaign for Congress in Florida's 1st Congressional District, eventually becoming the Democratic nominee in 2022.
Thousands of people who had supported my whistleblowing supported that campaign, too. About 14,000 people donated, helping us raise more than $850,000.
I knew it was an uphill race.
But after watching government fail so spectacularly during COVI, and seeing first-hand how easily institutions can be bent around the ambitions of people in power, I wasn't particularly interested in sitting quietly on the sidelines.
We didn't win.
But I don't regret running.
The experience fundamentally changed how I understood politics, journalism, and the enormous distance between the problems ordinary people live with and the things Washington chooses to spend its time fighting about.
That experience also helped shape what I do today.
## I went back to science.
Eventually, after three years of applications and rejections, I finally got a full-time job again.
I was doing the kind of work I had spent my entire adult life preparing to do.
And then Donald Trump returned to office.
Less than a year after I finally rebuilt some semblance of professional stability, the federal funding supporting my position was cancelled.
So I did what I've been doing since 2020.
I started over.
Again.
I found another position, this time with a UN-backed NGO, working in climate and ocean science.
That organization has now lost its funding, too.
So here I am again.
I don't know what comes next.
[Click here to subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/77f7902e-a41d-43ee-8d7d-0ffa2b06ef9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
## In the meantime, I built something of my own.
One of the most important things I've done since Florida is build an independent platform for the kind of work I believe matters.
That became **[Mesoscale News](https://substack.com/redirect/bfe0e9a0-da3d-411d-9c22-46349eb38975?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[.](https://substack.com/redirect/bfe0e9a0-da3d-411d-9c22-46349eb38975?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I've spent the last several years reporting and writing about climate change, disasters, public health, science, elections, democracy, and government accountability.
I've interviewed scientists, candidates, and public officials. I've investigated policy decisions and government actions. I've translated complicated scientific research into something people can actually use. I've covered hurricanes and wildfires, public-health threats and attacks on democratic institutions.
I've also built an audience that reaches millions of people.
And I've done it without surrendering the thing that started this entire journey in the first place:
The belief that facts matter.
Not because science is perfect. Not because scientists are infallible. And certainly not because institutions deserve unquestioning trust.
Facts matter because democracy cannot function without a shared reality.
That was true when Florida officials were deciding what COVID data the public was allowed to see.
It is even more true now.
[Click here to subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/77f7902e-a41d-43ee-8d7d-0ffa2b06ef9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
## And then there is the movie.
Josh Fox started documenting this story when it was still happening.
What began as a film about a scientist confronting the government over COVID data became something much larger, because the story itself became much larger.
It became a story about retaliation.
About family.
About the enormous personal cost of refusing to cooperate with something you believe is wrong.
About what happens after everyone applauds the whistleblower and goes home.
About trying to rebuild a career after becoming professionally radioactive.
About running for office because you've seen what happens when government stops working for the people it serves.
About raising kids while lawyers, politicians, police, reporters, and strangers on the internet fight over your life.
About continuing to believe that telling the truth matters even when doing so has cost you almost everything.
And, maybe most importantly, it is about what happens **after the headline**.
That's the part of whistleblower stories we rarely see.
We celebrate the moment someone speaks.
We don't usually stick around for year three.
Or year four.
Or year six.
Josh did.
## Now I want the people who made this possible to see it.
Many of you reading this were there before there was a documentary.
You helped pay lawyers.
You helped keep independent COVID data online.
You helped my family survive.
You wrote letters and emails. You defended me when doing so meant inviting abuse onto yourself. You donated $5 or $10 or $20 because you believed that somebody needed to stand up to what was happening.
Some of you probably haven't thought about me in years.
That's okay.
I haven't forgotten you.
And Josh hasn't forgotten that this movie exists in part because thousands of ordinary people decided this story mattered.
So he is sharing the film with those of you who helped make it happen.
## I wish this story ended with everything neatly working out.
It doesn't.
The future of the movie's wider release remains in limbo.
My professional future is uncertain again.
After three years of trying to find stable employment following my whistleblowing, I finally found it, only to have the funding cancelled less than a year later. I moved to another organization, and now that funding is gone, too.
Things are rough right now.
I don't know exactly where I'm headed from here.
But I know something that has been true since 2020:
**Your support makes the difference in whether I get to keep doing this work.**
If you followed what happened in Florida and wondered whatever became of that scientist with the COVID dashboard, well--
I'm still here.
Still doing science.
Still writing.
Still investigating.
Still getting into trouble.
Still refusing to shut up when something matters.
And still trying to figure out how to make that sustainable.
If you can, please consider becoming a paid subscriber to [my newsletter.](https://substack.com/redirect/bfe0e9a0-da3d-411d-9c22-46349eb38975?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) That support directly funds my reporting, science communication and independent work.
[Click here to subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/77f7902e-a41d-43ee-8d7d-0ffa2b06ef9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Or, if you're watching the documentary, consider donating what you might otherwise have spent going to see it in a theater -- the price of a couple of movie tickets, some gas, a babysitter, or an absurdly overpriced bucket of popcorn.
You can donate by [credit card or PayPal here](https://substack.com/redirect/404042c8-7115-4834-b20e-f6d7b0048fbc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), or via [Cashapp here.](https://substack.com/redirect/47982800-a475-41bb-a754-4f08da403e69?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
There are thousands of you who helped carry me through the worst period of my life.
Six years later, I'm asking for your help again.
Not because I want to keep reliving 2020.
Because there is still so much work left to do.
And because, despite everything that has happened since I first refused to change those numbers in Florida, I still believe the truth is worth fighting for.
**Thank you for being part of that fight.**

Cliff Schecter and David Shuster ask him everything. 2:00 p.m. Eastern.

I've spent this summer on the road, listening to folks talk about the challenges they're facing and what actually matters to them. All across the state, among farms, breweries, coffee shops, restaurants, community centers, churches and towns big and small, I hear a lot of similar stories. Grocery costs are too high, gas prices are rising, health care is an expensive problem and stuff just costs too much.
These conversations stick with me, and each story pushes me to continue fighting for a better North Carolina.
I've spent time in communities all across the state, and I'll continue visiting with people on the campaign trail (early voting starts in just 58 days). But between stops -- driving to events or a quick lunch break on a busy day -- I think about stories that inspire me, many of which come from books I've enjoyed reading during my life.
A story of great achievement that changed the world. A personal account of bigotry and abuse overcome by the power of writing extraordinary poetry and literature. A coach whose lessons about basketball provided courageous lessons about living a meaningful life. A world renowned scientist who explains the harmony between science and faith in God. A young lawyer who takes on a health insurance company that denies medical care.
Today, I wanted to share with you the books that tell these stories. These are books I've enjoyed and found meaningful:
1\. The Wright Brothers by David McCullough
2\. I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings by Maya Angelou
3\. A Coach's Life: My 40 Years in College Basketball by Dean Smith
4\. The Language of God by Dr. Francis Collins
5\. The Rainmaker by John Grisham
Of course there are many more, but these came to mind today. If you're enjoying a book or show this summer that might have affected or changed how you see things, I'd love to hear about it. Let me know in the comments. I might add it to my list!

**Hey folks - it's Roy Cooper.**
I've spent my life serving the people of North Carolina. As Governor, I expanded Medicaid to hundreds of thousands of hardworking people and fought for better health care. As Attorney General, I protected working families from fraud and abuse. As a State Legislator, I pushed for policies that made everyday people's lives easier.
But before all of this, I was just a boy from Nash County - the son of a public school teacher who tried to do right by his family, friends and neighbors.
Now, I'm running for the U.S. Senate because I've seen what's possible when government actually puts people first. When those in power lead with a sense of duty, purpose and moral clarity. That's not happening in Washington DC right now. **[Will you chip in today to help me change that?](https://substack.com/redirect/fc340344-f415-403f-834b-431590c7a78a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

# Join Our Autism Support Group
---
|
---
| We invite you to join us this **Wednesday, August 19th at 5:00 PM PST / 8:00 PM EST** via Zoom for an evening of encouragement, connection, and support. We know that caring for a child or loved one with autism can bring both incredible joys and significant challenges. Sometimes one of the most valuable resources is simply having a community of people who understand. Our Parent Support Group provides a space to learn from one another, discuss what is working for your family, hear the experiences of other parents, and build meaningful connections. **Advance registration is required to attend the Parent Support Group.** Please register using the Zoom link below to reserve your spot and receive the meeting information. We look forward to spending this time together and continuing to build a strong, informed, and supportive Autism Health community.
---
| [REGISTER HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/ppbyApgCLyz?e=3a42edfdc4&c2id=8db3279a53aa0d16c24f727ce5cda332 "REGISTER HERE")
---
|
---
|
# Help Shape the Future of Autism: We Need Your Voice
---
|
---
| The **Interagency Autism Coordinating Committee (IACC)** has released its **2026–2028 Working Draft Strategic Plan **for public comment. This is a rare opportunity for families, caregivers, clinicians, researchers, and advocates to help shape the future direction of autism research, healthcare, and federal services. **Your comments matter** The Working Draft outlines a comprehensive vision that addresses many of the challenges autism families have been asking our government to recognize for years. It includes greater attention to: \- The rising prevalence of autism and regressive autism
\- Co-occurring medical conditions, including gastrointestinal health, immune function, metabolism, sleep, and epilepsy
\- Neurodevelopmental regression and the need for additional research
\- Precision medicine and individualized approaches to care
\- Communication supports for nonspeaking and minimally speaking individuals
\- Improved diagnosis and access to clinical care
\- Caregiver support and respite services
\- Housing, employment, transportation, and aging across the lifespan
\- Greater accountability and coordination among federal agencies This Working Draft represents an important step toward addressing autism as a lifelong condition that requires comprehensive medical care, research, and family support. **Why We Need Positive Public Comments** The IACC is currently accepting public feedback before the Strategic Plan is finalized. If you believe these priorities are important, please take a few minutes to submit a respectful, positive comment. Public input helps demonstrate that autism families support continued progress in these areas and want to see these priorities reflected in future federal efforts. Your email doesn't need to be long. Simply share who you are, how autism has impacted your family, and why you support this Strategic Plan. Authentic, personal stories are far more meaningful than copied messages. Submit Your Comment to [**iaccpublicinquiries@mail.nih.gov**](mailto:iaccpublicinquiries@mail.nih.gov)
**Deadline:** **Thursday, August 20th** Below you'll find a button that will take you directly to the IACC webpage where you can learn more about the Working Draft and the public comment process. Together, our voices can help shape the future of autism research, healthcare, and support for generations to come. Thank you for taking a few moments to make your voice heard.
---

---

---
|
# Early Bird Registration for the Autism Health Summit
---
|
---
| The countdown has begun for the **2027 Autism Health Summit** , taking place **April 29 through May 1, 2027** , at **The Legacy Center Resort & Spa** in **San Diego, California**. Join parents, physicians, researchers, healthcare professionals, educators, and advocates from around the world for three inspiring days of education, collaboration, and hope. We're excited to announce that our **headline speakers** include **Del Bigtree** and **Dr. Henry Ealy** , with many more nationally recognized experts to be announced in the coming months. Attendees will gain valuable insights into the latest research, innovative therapies, integrative medicine, environmental health, and practical strategies to support individuals with autism and related neurological conditions. We're also pleased to offer **Continuing Medical Education (CME)** and **Continuing Education Unit (CEU)** credits for eligible healthcare professionals, making the Autism Health Summit an outstanding opportunity to expand your knowledge while earning valuable continuing education credits. **Now is the best time to register!** Secure your ticket before prices increase and receive **$50 OFF** your registration during the month of **August** by using promo code **AHS50** at checkout. This special offer expires at the end of the month. Whether you're a parent, caregiver, practitioner, educator, therapist, or advocate, the Autism Health Summit offers an unparalleled opportunity to learn from leading experts, connect with a passionate community, and leave empowered with practical knowledge you can apply immediately. **Reserve your seat today using the registration link below. We look forward to welcoming you to San Diego, April 29 through May 1, 2027!**

This is the perfect opportunity to showcase your organization while supporting one of the nation's premier autism education conferences.

# Join Us for Our Winter Gala!
---
|
---
| **Join Us for an Unforgettable Evening at the Autism Health Winter Gala** We are thrilled to invite you to the **First Annual Autism Health Winter Gala** , taking place on **Saturday, January 30, 2027** , at the beautiful **Trump National Golf Club in Jupiter, Florida**. This elegant evening will bring together supporters, physicians, researchers, community leaders, and families for a memorable celebration. Guests will enjoy an inspiring evening featuring a VIP reception, dinner, exciting live and silent auctions, and presentations from nationally recognized leaders. Your comments matter The Working Draft outlines a comprehensive vision that addresses many of the challenges autism families have been asking our government to recognize for years. It includes greater attention to: \- The rising prevalence of autism and regressive autism \- Co-occurring medical conditions, including gastrointestinal health, immune function, metabolism, sleep, and epilepsy \- Neurodevelopmental regression and the need for additional research \- Precision medicine and individualized approaches to care \- Communication supports for nonspeaking and minimally speaking individuals \- Improved diagnosis and access to clinical care \- Caregiver support and respite services \- Housing, employment, transportation, and aging across the lifespan \- Greater accountability and coordination among federal agencies This Working Draft represents an important step toward addressing autism as a lifelong condition that requires comprehensive medical care, research, and family support. name: Swing Left
subject: We can break 16 years of Republican control in Wisconsin’s state legislature
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft
body:
Democrats are just one governor’s race, two State Senate seats, and five State Assembly seats away from winning a trifecta.
#
Hi there,
This November, Swing Left is going all in on statewide races—and Wisconsin is one of the places where we’re focusing our efforts.
Democratic Governor Tony Evers is not seeking re-election, and **David Crowley** has won the Democratic nomination to keep this critical swing state governorship blue. He’ll face Republican **Tom Tiffany** this November, who has been in lockstep with Donald Trump in Congress and even backed his efforts to throw out the results of the 2020 election.
Wisconsin’s governor has veto power over the legislative maps that will shape the state’s political map for the next decade, which means that holding this seat is essential to keeping Republicans from drawing themselves a structural advantage before 2028.
But holding the governor’s office is just one part of the plan.
Democrats haven’t held a majority in either the State Senate or State Assembly since the Republican landslide in the 2010 midterm election. Republican legislators then used their majorities to implement what some experts called “the most gerrymandered maps in the country”, ensuring Republican control of the state legislature for years. But the Wisconsin Supreme Court struck down those maps, and in 2024, new, fairer state legislative maps were passed, meaning Democrats have a meaningful chance to win back control.
**Democrats are just one governor’s race, two State Senate seats, and five State Assembly seats away from winning a trifecta for the first time since Republicans first took over in 2011, and together, we can help make it happen.**
[](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-states-wi-2026.8VFGXY&refcode=em20260818-2486&t=1&akid=2486%2E1562180%2EQrOwn8) | [](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-states-wi-2026.8VFGXY&refcode=em20260818-2486&t=2&akid=2486%2E1562180%2EQrOwn8)
---|---
State legislative control also provides an essential governing anchor should Democrats lose the governor’s race. Flipping one or both chambers would allow Democrats to block conservative overreach, protect hard-won progress, and ensure Republicans cannot govern unchecked.
[**If you’re ready to support state-level races in Wisconsin, will you make a donation to our Wisconsin Win In The States Fund today?**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-states-wi-2026.8VFGXY&refcode=em20260818-2486&t=3&akid=2486%2E1562180%2EQrOwn8) **Your dollars will go to David Crowley’s campaign for governor, the Democratic legislative caucus campaign arms in Wisconsin, and Swing Left to support our organizing efforts in competitive races.**
**[Donate Now](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-states-wi-2026.8VFGXY&refcode=em20260818-2486&t=4&akid=2486%2E1562180%2EQrOwn8)**
Thank you as always for everything you do,
The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20260818-1&t=5&refcode2=2486_1562180_QrOwn8&akid=2486%2E1562180%2EQrOwn8)

body:
Peter,
I’m reaching out personally, because this Wednesday - on August 19th - our campaign will face **our final FEC deadline before New Hampshire’s primary election.**
**[If you’re in a position to help our campaign in a major way by chipping in your first $5 split between us and Tammy Baldwin before this major deadline, it’d mean so much.](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/6050?c0=em-ms-tb-20260818-pappas.ve-zxJ&amount=5&refcode=em20260818-5605&t=1&akid=5605%2E35263%2ELF2JKB)**
Look, Peter, this deadline is different from our usual monthly and quarterly deadlines I’ve emailed you about before. And I want to tell you exactly why:
Wednesday’s deadline marks the LAST time we’ll report our fundraising to the FEC before the primary election. That means it’s our LAST chance to prove we can defeat the MAGA billionaires who are dumping money into this race to try to buy the Granite State’s Senate seat.
It’s no exaggeration to say this is the biggest test our campaign has faced so far. And our ability to keep New Hampshire’s Senate seat blue and flip control of the Senate will come down to whether we can raise enough to build a winning campaign.
**We need to take this opportunity to show the size and strength of this grassroots team, so I’m humbly asking:**
**[Please, Peter, rush a donation of any amount right now split between our campaign and Tammy Baldwin so we can reach our fundraising goal before Wednesday’s deadline and prove that our campaign is stronger than ever.](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/6050?c0=em-ms-tb-20260818-pappas.ve-zxJ&amount=5&refcode=em20260818-5605&t=2&akid=5605%2E35263%2ELF2JKB)**
Right now Republicans are outspending us at a ratio of 3 to 1. They’re counting on us to be intimidated by their spending; they believe that flooding the airwaves will discourage our campaign from moving forward.
This FEC deadline is our final opportunity before the primary for us to show that we have the support needed to win here in New Hampshire.
With your help our FEC report will prove that we have the support of everyday folks like you. Together we can prove that New Hampshire is not for sale.
**[So, Peter, what do you say? Will you step up for the first time to help us defend New Hampshire and flip the Senate blue?](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/6050?c0=em-ms-tb-20260818-pappas.ve-zxJ&amount=5&refcode=em20260818-5605&t=3&akid=5605%2E35263%2ELF2JKB)**

Thank you for all that you do,
Chris Pappas

Peter, it's Becca. **This morning, I was thinking about what happened 106 years ago today. On August 18, 1920, the 19th Amendment was ratified.** Generations of women organized, marched, fought, and refused to accept that they should have no say in the decisions shaping their own lives. **And more than a century later, I don’t take that victory for granted for one second.** Because while today is an anniversary worth celebrating, it’s also a reminder that progress does not simply protect itself. We are living through a moment when fundamental rights we once thought were settled are being challenged again. We have already watched reproductive freedom stripped away across the country. We have watched attacks on voting rights continue. And we are hearing rhetoric about women and our place in society that belongs firmly in the past. [_**If you believe, like I do, that our job is to protect the progress generations before us fought so hard to win, I’d be so grateful if you’d chip in $10, $25, or whatever feels right today to help me keep fighting for it.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137465643/640881836/687315491?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MzUxMmM4OS0yYTliLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Y8ceZNYLhmrv7E5UXun3ilzey_nBvOGPMufHs9eN4pc=) **[CLICK HERE TO CHIP IN TODAY!](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137465644/640881837/687315491?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MzUxMmM4OS0yYTliLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Y8ceZNYLhmrv7E5UXun3ilzey_nBvOGPMufHs9eN4pc=)** **I refuse to accept that going backward is our future.** _I’m the first woman and first openly LGBTQ+ person Vermont has ever sent to Congress. I carry that history with me every single day, because I know none of us gets here alone._ People before us fought like hell to open doors they would never get to walk through themselves. **Our job is to make sure those doors stay open, and then open them wider for the people coming next.** [_**And since I’m writing to friends here, I’ll just ask plainly: if you believe in what I’m fighting for, would you consider making a contribution today?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137465645/640881838/687315491?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MzUxMmM4OS0yYTliLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Y8ceZNYLhmrv7E5UXun3ilzey_nBvOGPMufHs9eN4pc=) So yes, today I’m celebrating. But I’m also recommitting myself to the work ahead. We will protect the right to vote, our freedoms, and the progress generations before us fought so hard to win. **And we are not going to let anyone drag us backward.** With so much gratitude, — Becca

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. There's a battle for your bottom line. Corporations planned it, you feel it—but they've spent billions making sure you can't name it. They conceal, they confuse, they rebrand—but it all leads to the same goal: more of your money in their pocket, less of their product in yours. Remember watching your grandfather work on his all-steel, American-made car or truck with just a few simple tools? Somewhere along the way, corporations stopped seeing a great American machine to be proud of and started seeing lost revenue potential. Today, vehicles are an assortment of cheap plastic, complicated electronics, and systems so complex that routine maintenance like changing the battery feels impossible. That's by design. They engineer a car you can't work on so that every breakdown costs you more—and your problem becomes their payday. Moms were some of the first to notice corporations were messing with time-tested products. Whether it was shrinking portion sizes or replacing natural ingredients with unpronounceable chemicals, moms felt it long before terms like shrinkflation, slack-fill, and reformulation became household words. Grocery budgets today don't go nearly as far as they did just a few years ago—and the gap keeps growing. The latest corporate attack on the bottom line is already here—surveillance pricing. We can't always see it, but we have hard evidence of the pain surveillance pricing causes at grocery stores and airlines. In fact, we don't even know the full scope, because the algorithms are intentionally opaque and unaccountable. Massive retailers are hiring AI companies to build a file on you: your shopping history, your location, and your family details. They use it to charge you a different price than the person standing next to you for the exact same item. We've all seen the stories of Silicon Valley snapping up farms all across America's heartland to build massive data centers. They're not there to feed your AI searches. They're built to fuel the next wave of AI implementation, not for consumers, but against them. I'm sounding the alarm, because a country where a small group of the rich and powerful preys on the working class is a country in crisis. It's already happening, but I'm fighting to stop it. Just as those great American companies lost their way, too many in Washington have lost theirs. The interests of the God-fearing, tax-paying, family-raising majority of Middle America have been displaced—and far too many on both sides of the aisle are motivated by money that flows freely from the massive corporations headquartered on both coasts. Not me. I'll fight this battle because it's right—but I don't have to fight it alone. I know there are American patriots out there, tired of being overlooked by Washington and exploited by corporations, who feel every dollar of the financial strain that corporations engineered and Washington ignored. No more. [**Stand with me. Max-out contributions not required—this campaign is fueled by $5, $10, and $25 donations from people who've had enough. clean_body: | | | | | | | Peter, There's a battle for your bottom line. Corporations planned it, you feel it—but they've spent billions making sure you can't name it. They conceal, they confuse, they rebrand—but it all leads to the same goal: more of your money in their pocket, less of their product in yours. Remember watching your grandfather work on his all-steel, American-made car or truck with just a few simple tools? Somewhere along the way, corporations stopped seeing a great American machine to be proud of and started seeing lost revenue potential. Today, vehicles are an assortment of cheap plastic, complicated electronics, and systems so complex that routine maintenance like changing the battery feels impossible. That's by design. They engineer a car you can't work on so that every breakdown costs you more—and your problem becomes their payday. Moms were some of the first to notice corporations were messing with time-tested products. Whether it was shrinking portion sizes or replacing natural ingredients with unpronounceable chemicals, moms felt it long before terms like shrinkflation, slack-fill, and reformulation became household words. Grocery budgets today don't go nearly as far as they did just a few years ago—and the gap keeps growing. The latest corporate attack on the bottom line is already here—surveillance pricing. We can't always see it, but we have hard evidence of the pain surveillance pricing causes at grocery stores and airlines. In fact, we don't even know the full scope, because the algorithms are intentionally opaque and unaccountable. Massive retailers are hiring AI companies to build a file on you: your shopping history, your location, and your family details. They use it to charge you a different price than the person standing next to you for the exact same item. We've all seen the stories of Silicon Valley snapping up farms all across America's heartland to build massive data centers. They're not there to feed your AI searches. They're built to fuel the next wave of AI implementation, not for consumers, but against them. I'm sounding the alarm, because a country where a small group of the rich and powerful preys on the working class is a country in crisis. It's already happening, but I'm fighting to stop it. Just as those great American companies lost their way, too many in Washington have lost theirs. The interests of the God-fearing, tax-paying, family-raising majority of Middle America have been displaced—and far too many on both sides of the aisle are motivated by money that flows freely from the massive corporations headquartered on both coasts. Not me. I'll fight this battle because it's right—but I don't have to fight it alone. I know there are American patriots out there, tired of being overlooked by Washington and exploited by corporations, who feel every dollar of the financial strain that corporations engineered and Washington ignored. No more. | | In Liberty, Senator Josh Hawley | | | | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|--- Paid for by Josh Hawley Victory Committee | | | |

[ stdin# ]Our Revolution Logo

Peter Willis,

The Israeli strikes on Lebanon have not stopped, despite the supposed
ceasefire. Eleven people were killed last weekend in the worst attacks
since the ceasefire went into effect.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39498?source=email-20260818&t=1011&akid=11207%2E5885482%2Ew3fMIZ ]Headline: Eleven killed in Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon,
authorities say

Instead of using its leverage to demand that Netanyahu stop the violence,
Congress is rushing to REWARD the Israeli government with a new provision
in the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) that all but fuses our
two militaries.

The House already passed it before heading home for recess and the Senate
could soon follow. As violence rages, we must show Congress there is
massive opposition to this dangerous escalation of U.S.-Israeli military
ties. Now is the time to make it clear that the public will not stand by
and allow Section 219 to become law.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39498?source=email-20260818&t=1012&akid=11207%2E5885482%2Ew3fMIZ ]Add your name now: Tell the Senate to strip Section 219 from the NDAA
before it’s too late!

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39498?source=email-20260818&t=1013&akid=11207%2E5885482%2Ew3fMIZ ]ADD YOUR NAME

Section 219 was written by lobbyists and Netanyahu himself. It would
supersize weapons deals, surveillance tech, and intelligence sharing for
years to come, stripping away even the limited Congressional checks that
exist today.

AOC has made the risks of merging the U.S. and Israel’s
military-technology industrial complexes clear, saying that it poses an
“existential threat” to U.S. democracy.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39498?source=email-20260818&t=1014&akid=11207%2E5885482%2Ew3fMIZ ]Headline: AOC: US-Israeli Military Integration Measure “Existential
Threat” to Democracy

Now we ALL need to come together to stop it — and there’s a clear path.

Since the bill already passed the House, our next chance is to stop it is
in the Senate. Last month, Democrats in the Senate blocked debate on the
NDAA because of Trump’s war on Iran. But now pressure is mounting for the
Senate to pass the NDAA when it returns from recess — and it’s up to ALL
of us to make it clear where we stand.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39498?source=email-20260818&t=1015&akid=11207%2E5885482%2Ew3fMIZ ]Take action now. Add your name to send a loud, unified message to the
