# **[AI's $3 trillion off-balance-sheet time bomb finally goes mainstream](https://substack.com/redirect/de4c36e8-987e-4a87-8a9c-3b06bb779ad9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
WSJ finally sees what got flagged months ago. Nine big tech names now carry $3 trillion in off-balance-sheet AI commitments, up $1.2 trillion in a single quarter. Uncommenced leases alone hit $1.2 trillion. Purchase obligations another $1.9 trillion. Meta's Hyperion stays hidden until the rent checks start. Capex was the tip. The real tab lives in the footnotes. Exactly the spend reckoning we called when **[Google got punished for spending like a drunken sailor](https://substack.com/redirect/58cd50f5-cd65-4ae9-88db-1e1cd62d3a85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on AI and the $2 trillion chip carnage slammed into support.
* **Winners?** Nvidia locking the $500 billion private-credit backstop. Suppliers who get paid whether the models monetize or not. Chinese open-weight models crushing token prices more than 50% and grabbing share with dirt-cheap compute.
* **Losers?** Hyperscalers running negative free cash flow while the depreciation wall still sits in construction-in-progress. Pure-play labs still burning cash. Anyone long the multiple without reading the lease footnotes.
* **Next?** Margins get crushed when the deferred depreciation lands. More SPVs or a funding window that suddenly shuts. Token price war accelerates if Chinese models keep undercutting.

They hid the leverage in the footnotes while the Street celebrated the supercycle. Now the bill is visible and private credit is the layer funding half of it. Sentiment still lets them raise. When that window closes the only question left is who still has real cash flow. Greed was good. Visibility is better. The weak get flushed. The disciplined collect.

# **[Photonics is printing while copper fries itself into toast](https://substack.com/redirect/de4c36e8-987e-4a87-8a9c-3b06bb779ad9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Don't believe me? Who chooses copper over fiber optic for home broadband? Same deal here, just on a giant scale. Optics is the only pavement that moves data across million-square-foot AI data centers without melting. Copper is a toaster oven. Nearly $700 billion in hyperscaler spend has no choice. Photonics and optics just posted 113% gains in 2026 while the MSCI All Country World Index crawls at 14%. Bank of America crowned it the best global theme of the year and top-quintile triple momentum. Tema's brand-new LAZR ETF ripped 34% this month on Coherent and Lumentum.
* **Winners?** Coherent, Lumentum, LAZR holders and every pure optical interconnect name collecting tolls on the AI clusters. Light moves farther, cooler, faster. The smart money that bought the unglamorous layer early.
* **Losers?** Copper cable dinosaurs, FOMO chasers paying 35-42 times forward earnings, and anyone still pretending traditional wires scale these monsters. They're about to get cooked.
* **Next?** The bad day for copper is coming. Wait for the wave, load the pure plays hard, then ride co-packaged optics and photonic chips as the $700 billion keeps flowing into denser clusters.

Exactly as I flagged in **["UMC fires up Singapore production for AI photonics as Citi turns bullish"](https://substack.com/redirect/a43e051c-6695-497c-a264-3cb7eb8b3c91?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** inside the Apple lawsuit piece, silicon photonics is the quiet killer app of AI scale. The numbers are now screaming it. High multiples demand predator discipline, buy the fear, not the greed. Optics doesn't care which model you're running. It's mandatory pavement. Get positioned or get left holding melted copper while the light-speed trade compounds. Greed works when it's pointed at the actual bottleneck.

body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
When it comes to Donald Trump and the MAGA Extremists, one thing is absolutely certain: The grift never, EVER stops.
Right now, the head of the United States Postal Service is doing Donald Trump's dirty work — implementing an executive order that federal courts have already ruled unconstitutional. Twice.
Here's what's happening:
Trump signed an executive order aimed at controlling how election mail is handled in this country — an order two separate federal courts have already blocked as unconstitutional. Most people would call that settled. Postmaster General David Steiner didn't.
Now, Postmaster General Steiner refuses to tell Congress whether his agency is complying with a federal court order. Even after the injunction. Even after the First Circuit ruled against Trump again on July 25th.
Let's call this exactly what it is: The United States Postal Service — an institution that is supposed to serve every American equally, no matter their zip code or their politics — has been turned into a partisan instrument of voter suppression.
This is deliberate. Trump wants control over how your ballot gets delivered, and he found someone running USPS who's willing to give it to him — court orders be damned.
I sent Steiner a letter demanding answers. I want to know every step USPS has taken to implement this order, every piece of guidance sent to postal workers, and exactly why he thinks he's above two federal court rulings. The Democrat Senatorial Campaign Committee issued multiple statements of support for Islamic communist US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed just hours after Haley Stevens conceded Michigan's Democrat U.S. Senate primary election to him. The endorsement comes as the DSCC has opened joint fundraising committees with Senate candidates Sherrod Brown of Ohio, Jon Ossoff of Georgia, Alex Vindman of Florida, and James Talarico of Texas - all of whom are attempting to run their races in Trump-won states as "moderates." El-Sayed and his extremist friends are anything but moderates and their exactly the kind of far-left candidates the DSCC loves endorsing.

The DSCC released a joint statement from Senate Democrat Leader Chuck Schumer and DSCC Chair Kirsten Gillibrand announcing their support for El-Sayed, which reads in part:
> _" Democrats are united by a common purpose: putting a check on Donald Trump by defeating his Republican enablers and taking back the Senate. We look forward to working with Abdul and Democrats across Michigan to win this seat in November."_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/177c50e6-c73e-49b5-897c-3d131526e950?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

---|---|---
The DSCC also promoted El-Sayed on its official X account, posting:
> _" BREAKING: Dr. Abdul El-Sayed is officially the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Michigan! A born-and-raised Michigander, @AbdulElSayed has inspired thousands of Michiganders across the state. Now he's going to the Senate to keep fighting for affordable health care and lower costs."_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d2d12f2a-5dde-4720-8302-41c85fb12c74?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Absent from the DSCC's celebration of the "born-and-raised Michigander" is any mention that El-Sayed spent his summers in Egypt and [has praised the Muslim Brotherhood](https://substack.com/redirect/1a1a39e4-e0f1-498e-ad34-38f60683e8e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), as Loomered exclusively reported.
The endorsement comes as the DSCC works to build joint fundraising committees with candidates in Trump-won states who are campaigning as "moderates." In Ohio, Sherrod Brown's Ohio Senate Victory 2026 committee links Friends of Sherrod Brown directly with the DSCC.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b231c3a4-549d-4732-81a1-2165d07a0372?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Brown has also [created two joint fundraising committees with James Talarico](https://substack.com/redirect/6d11f34c-d596-4ee8-88d3-a4e390bc6189?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in an apparent attempt to transform Ohio.

Many conservatives point to this as a warning against bad immigration policies, arguing that we must fight to stop this from happening here. Well, I have some bad news: IT ALREADY DID HAPPEN HERE! Under Biden, our Southern Border was WIDE OPEN, and millions of foreign nationals flooded our country illegally. It’s not some distant news story; it was our REALITY for FOUR YEARS! And if Democrats take back power, this is what the Southern Border will look like. That’s not a guess, it’s not an exaggeration, it’s a fact. We all saw it with our own eyes. | I’ve always fought to keep our communities safe through strong border policies. But that goal of protecting our wives, children, and neighbors from the dangers of illegal immigration is not shared by the Democrats. In fact, we’ve seen that the Democrats WANT open borders. They WANT illegal immigrants to flood our country. They WANT to give them welfare and YOUR job. I’m running against a radical open-border Democrat who wants to defund ICE and reopen our borders; I need some support. It's called **_Texas Cares_** and here’s what it does: **Expands Medicaid** for Texans living under 138% of the poverty line. _The same coverage Texas GOP leadership has refused for twelve years_. **Creates Lone Star Basic** for working Texans who earn too much for Medicaid and too little to afford private insurance. _Nobody should fall between the cracks when it comes to healthcare. _ **Creates Lone Star Preferred:** a state-run insurance option open to every Texan, where coverage decisions get made based on what's best for patients, not what maximizes profits. Your annual checkup costs you nothing. No copay. No deductible. Children get covered first. **Dan Patrick has had a decade to tackle the healthcare crisis...** Instead, he blocked Medicaid expansion. That’s costing Texas $10 billion a year — over **$100 BILLION** of our tax money that we sent to Washington, _then handed to other states._ He decided that scoring a political point was worth more than covering 5.1 million Texans. This morning in Houston, we released our plan to cover every one of them. = Texas Cares press conference with (left to right) Representative Christina Morales, Tyler Smith, and Dr. Letitia Plummer It's called Texas Cares and here’s what it does: Expands Medicaid for Texans living under 138% of the poverty line. The same coverage Texas GOP leadership has refused for twelve years. Creates Lone Star Basic for working Texans who earn too much for Medicaid and too little to afford private insurance. Nobody should fall between the cracks when it comes to healthcare. Creates Lone Star Preferred: a state-run insurance option open to every Texan, where coverage decisions get made based on what's best for patients, not what maximizes profits. Your annual checkup costs you nothing. No copay. No deductible. Children get covered first. Dan Patrick has had a decade to tackle the healthcare crisis... Instead, he blocked Medicaid expansion. | | | Peter, Right now, well-paid DC consultants and TV talking heads are arguing that the best way to beat MAGA extremists in swing districts is to cling to the centrist status quo. _**They’re wrong.**_ And we have the numbers to back it up. We released new research the other week from 18 toss-up districts showing that voters — especially independents — are rewarding candidates who promise to change the system, not protect it. [](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9-dEPsMTCXuEE1CGpCIrSol1icujQnVva7d3CIDGFSVEOP3lwh_mj-sOzUhnxefkM9XSOXO4RYTBe4Df8qBUoNs0BsL5RcZUqVtpktLbFEBrPsCFpNZ8GHeE49zLCvAlt9cIMBLQenyO8GujQK_IjrOaDNOzvbLKJ74Ls48_uZgnd8Chcu0Wq1RMsGsWEIQAABEPD3SwuwgXGaJj82nqlyIKEInHI5BAgZRjJDywhwwV1_poYzgUPA4G_GkbmN9qGI2A3w8HRDLVBx5ZuMe9YPl2kexuDvb0ammjp1TyLY_I/4ta/FVzEh9h0T9GdDGKnBIpI9Q/h0/h001.nWxFG7WujK2Q1tclRdYCjMpDc2gccDBovwENsErU2rI) And we’re seeing the reality of this anti-establishment sentiment in elections across the country. From **Randy Villegas** in California, to **Bob Brooks** in Pennsylvania, to **Abdul El-Sayed** and **Will Lawrence** in Michigan last week, in race after race, the change candidate running on a populist message is winning, even against tens of millions of dollars in ugly attack ads. At the Working Families Party, we take pride in recruiting, training, and supporting leaders with the guts and the vision to build a government that works for the people over the powerful. But the problem with standing up to the corporate establishment is that they have millions in corporate money behind them to drown out our message, to try and convince voters that change is impossible or scary. With 11 weeks until the midterm elections, we need your help to break through the establishment noise and show voters what Working Families Party candidates across the country are fighting for. **[Can we count on you to make a weekly recurring donation from now until Election Day on November 3? Even a few dollars a week goes a long way in funding our organizing and voter outreach in these swing districts.](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9-dEPsMTCXuEE1CGpCIrSol1icujQnVva7d3CIDGFSVEOP3lwh_mj-sOzUhnxefkMeUhjV8wT0SH2QVWPZOSNtP1vqn9lsxxb2Owel0vMf_OPdnYj-cRk5dHz_IjKNLTFLHzjVbv5keHa-6gFJSuoiUu149j96RUUmDC1Ueg6Tvfmq2c16A2JuKwXTYQdzSj-RwHnp_ymP9CiyYQF114noflNsbnorXK9UXt2UrGzOiz-Y7tIbi9yPz3GAdLHxut3UIQ218O9zGOnjsUOFyoryWwrtrN6aYLdQJ8gFb94uvQ/4ta/FVzEh9h0T9GdDGKnBIpI9Q/h1/h001.QUb6SkrFHrM9nezZe1Hf6ujPkVFe1AWM7hlFxyiTc0Q)** **[Make a weekly donation](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9-dEPsMTCXuEE1CGpCIrSol1icujQnVva7d3CIDGFSVEOP3lwh_mj-sOzUhnxefkMI_3TQty3mmWz0pWw6tAP7y9co3YtdspF-yAH-tonlIZrhJXOdJ48lc0fRyJnnk3uOX3SnZDKSMn_5X-9pbj7oDBsQJaO_ya1-PDVjKWxkYZOQCoPH_hRDeAV2qRUAABfUo8OVmobx7LccnJGblvW6_O9YACdYL-BOyC6EW9VK4f_5JvhJdbx9vhCOEPpPZke2Q7Pu3pl8vq3_SSe0I-kGzsWqDr5dS5ksGotjsjM3Q0/4ta/FVzEh9h0T9GdDGKnBIpI9Q/h2/h001.FciEE7b3B9oWZ0BUzlX_JC-H2ExZqP4CgiS61riXnHQ)** **What we found when we talked to swing-district voters was striking:**
* 80% of swing-district voters agree that elected officials care more about wealthy interests than people like them.
* 67% of swing-district voters would be more likely to vote for a candidate who will challenge leaders of their own party.
* 64% of swing-district voters want to vote for a candidate who pushes for major change, even if it disrupts the usual way of doing things.
* More than half of swing district voters support putting an end to U.S.-led wars, making it easier for workers to form unions, and raising taxes on wealthy people and large corporations.

Our data reflects what we see on the ground every day — that the corporate establishment has created a system where the cost of living is out of control, where big business is given free reign to abuse working people for the sake of profits, where the wealthiest people in this country hoard the very resources that could lift up our communities. And voters are sick and tired of it. This midterm season is our opportunity to harness that energy and replace MAGA extremists with leaders from all backgrounds who will fight a broken status quo. It’s an opportunity we cannot waste. **[Click here to make a weekly recurring donation from now until November 3. clean_body: | | | Peter, Right now, well-paid DC consultants and TV talking heads are arguing that the best way to beat MAGA extremists in swing districts is to cling to the centrist status quo. They’re wrong. And we have the numbers to back it up. We released new research the other week from 18 toss-up districts showing that voters — especially independents — are rewarding candidates who promise to change the system, not protect it. And we’re seeing the reality of this anti-establishment sentiment in elections across the country. From Randy Villegas in California, to Bob Brooks in Pennsylvania, to Abdul El-Sayed and Will Lawrence in Michigan last week, in race after race, the change candidate running on a populist message is winning, even against tens of millions of dollars in ugly attack ads. At the Working Families Party, we take pride in recruiting, training, and supporting leaders with the guts and the vision to build a government that works for the people over the powerful. But the problem with standing up to the corporate establishment is that they have millions in corporate money behind them to drown out our message, to try and convince voters that change is impossible or scary. With 11 weeks until the midterm elections, we need your help to break through the establishment noise and show voters what Working Families Party candidates across the country are fighting for. What we found when we talked to swing-district voters was striking: 80% of swing-district voters agree that elected officials care more about wealthy interests than people like them. 67% of swing-district voters would be more likely to vote for a candidate who will challenge leaders of their own party. 64% of swing-district voters want to vote for a candidate who pushes for major change, even if it disrupts the usual way of doing things. More than half of swing district voters support putting an end to U.S.-led wars, making it easier for workers to form unions, and raising taxes on wealthy people and large corporations. Our data reflects what we see on the ground every day — that the corporate establishment has created a system where the cost of living is out of control, where big business is given free reign to abuse working people for the sake of profits, where the wealthiest people in this country hoard the very resources that could lift up our communities. And voters are sick and tired of it. This midterm season is our opportunity to harness that energy and replace MAGA extremists with leaders from all backgrounds who will fight a broken status quo. It’s an opportunity we cannot waste. In solidarity, Working Families Party Thoughts? Feedback? We want to hear it. Reply directly to this email and let us know. body:
[ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor
Hi there,

We’re coming up on our next big fundraising deadline, and we could use
your help.
[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/12677?t=1001&akid=1800%2E181023%2EqEe1P1 ]Will
you step up today and make your first contribution to help us start off
the general election strong?

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/12677?t=1002&akid=1800%2E181023%2EqEe1P1 ]Donate →

We know that was direct, but this is one of the
most important governor’s races in the country. If you need to hear more
before making a generous contribution, here’s why your support ahead of
our critical goal is so crucial:

📊 The latest polls show this race is going to be extremely close. Jocelyn
is in the lead, but in a battleground state like Michigan, we can’t get
overconfident.
💰 Republicans are pouring everything they have into defeating

* * *
_**by David Shuster**_
There is something particularly insane these days about Donald Trump's approach toward statesmanship. On top of having the biggest microphone in the world and possessing the loudest and most obnoxious voice, Trump is now promoting the U.S. nuclear arsenal and mistaking intimidation for strategy.
Alarm bells are ringing not just because Trump has been waging war against Iran with the subtlety of a sledgehammer. According to former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene, Trump has discussed with other administration officials the possibility of using nuclear weapons against Iran.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1b69e196-b32b-4c8d-8747-9d55f3513dd2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Greene is not exactly the most rational or credible or source on the U.S. political scene. So anything she says or claims deserves skepticism. But several news outlets reported similar Trump discussions in May, prompting Trump to issue a public denial. Three months later, with Iran as defiant as ever, Trump has reportedly circled back to talking about nuclear weapons and seems willing to have the Iranian regime think he is crazy enough to actually consider using such weapons. And that begs the question. Why is a U.S. President allowing anybody in Iran or elsewhere to wonder whether Trump's negotiating repertoire includes nuclear attack?
Again, perhaps the whole thing is merely psychological warfare. Maybe Trump thinks that he can frighten Tehran, rattle the regime's cages, and make the leadership believe he is so reckless and crazy that Iran should agree to open the Strait of Hormuz with no tolls and end the global energy shock before Trump considers an atomic shock.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1b69e196-b32b-4c8d-8747-9d55f3513dd2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Still, even the irrational actor strategy Trump may be floating is a grotesquely bad idea. Nuclear weapons are not ordinary diplomatic tools. They are not the verbal equivalent of "very," "tremendous," or "the biggest." They are instruments capable of killing millions of civilians in a flash, contaminating territory, provoking retaliation and transforming a conventional war into World War Three.
Also, the threat could fail in several ways. The enemy could call the bluff. The enemy can misunderstand it. An ally could misunderstand it. A subordinate could misunderstand it. A radar operator could misunderstand something on a screen. A military commander could conclude that the president has crossed a threshold that everyone else assumed Trump was merely pretending to approach.
This is why nuclear deterrence has always depended upon something Trump seems to lack: seriousness. The problem is not just that Trump says outrageous things. Outrage is his native language. The problem is that he has attached outrageous language to actual military power.
Here's the part that should keep you up at night.
It doesn't matter whether Trump is bluffing. It matters whether Tehran can tell.

They've been building the resources to fight exactly this kind of late-race scramble, and they're not going to sit back and let these seats slip away quietly. Playing defense and ceding ground to Republicans is what got us here. Going on offense is how we win. name: Carleigh Beriont
subject: We are Musk and Zuckʼs worst nightmare.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Carleigh Beriont for Congress
body:
They just donʼt know it yet.

| |
---
| | Dear David, Our lives have become beholden to the priorities and profits of technology corporations, and we never had a say in it. You can’t pay for parking, get into a movie, or do basic tasks without your phone. AI is accelerating this problem: it is being used to deny people healthcare, replace workers, surveil communities, and make military decisions that should require human judgment. The Pentagon is integrating AI into operations faster than lawmakers can provide oversight, and **the companies building these systems have amassed so much power that they can pay for whatever laws they want.** Weʼve seen this story before. Social media companies were allowed to grow for twenty years without any meaningful regulation. We have just started to see accountability for these companies after they wreaked havoc on our public health and democracy for decades. These are the same tech companies that designed products to addict children and failed to protect kids from predators on their platforms. **I donʼt want to wait another twenty years for class action lawsuits against AI companies to finally deliver justice for their victims, when we can act now to prevent these harms from occurring in the first place.** That’s why I support a moratorium on data center construction until we have legislation that requires these companies to address and offset the impact of new data centers on public health, the environment, and energy prices; gives people a choice on whether or not these centers get built in their communities; and subjects corporations to aggressive antitrust enforcement and robust data privacy protections. But a data center moratorium just scratches the surface of this problem. We need and we deserve so much more. I promise you that I will not rest until we:
* Protect your privacy online the way we protect our mail.
* Break up these monopolies and take away their control of our politics.
* Ensure the prosperity created by artificial intelligence is shared with the working people who helped to build it and keep it running.

**[I’m someone who is fighting to regulate AI _now_ rather than waiting for the harms later. # **San Francisco high school with highest Berkley acceptance rate has 94% of students flunking math**
Mission High School in San Francisco had a 45% UC Berkeley acceptance rate last fall -- triple the state average -- despite only 17% of 11th graders scoring proficient in English and just 6% in math on 2025 state exams, **[the lowest in the district.](https://substack.com/redirect/7ce6960d-57f7-4613-9daa-f46e1073586b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

---|---|---
* **Critics attribute the gap to lax grading standards** and UC's 2020 decision to drop SAT/ACT requirements, which they say lets underprepared students into rigorous courses; only half of Mission High's UC-bound students graduate within four years.
* **The disparity has fueled faculty calls to restore standardized testing,** with UC Berkeley and UC San Diego professors describing students years behind in math. A UC Berkeley spokesperson confirmed Mission's elevated acceptance rate but denied targeting any specific school.

A single-payer healthcare system like Medicare-for-All would save an incredible amount of lives and money in America.
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2438%2E791427%2E1013x8)
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-aug26.wDIP7w&refcode=em260818-1-180&t=2&akid=2438%2E791427%2E1013x8)
Friend — another important study has shown what many of us have already known:
**A single-payer healthcare system like Medicare-for-All would save an incredible amount of lives and money in America.**
Look, when progressives advocate for Medicare-for-All, we always get asked, “how will you pay for it?” But nobody ever asks how we are possibly affording our current system.
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-aug26.wDIP7w&refcode=em260818-1-180&t=3&akid=2438%2E791427%2E1013x8)
Our for-profit healthcare system costs **_far more_** than systems around the world that guarantee healthcare as a human right. And who’s paying that extra cost? All of us.
As the Yale study writes: “Healthcare costs have been rising faster than inflation, and a staggering share of that spending is consumed by administrative middlemen, soaring drug prices, and emergency care for conditions that should have been treated earlier and for less.”
The political establishment and the corporate media have a financial interest in making Medicare-for-All sound like some crazy idea, but the reality couldn’t be more different: Medicare-for-All is the cost-efficient, affordable, effective, and reliable healthcare solution that Americans are desperate for.
That establishment is the only thing standing between us and saving over 100,000 lives and $1 trillion a year. The job of our movement is to fight for this common-sense idea in the face of massive opposition from the billionaire class.
Keep fighting, keep organizing, and never let them tell you that Medicare-for-All is too risky of an idea. The only risk is continuing the status quo and wasting more money and lives so the rich can keep getting richer.
In solidarity,
Team Ilhan

* * *

**Before you go!**
Ilhan Omar has fought to pass Medicare-for-All since the day she first got to Congress. Now, she’s working to elect progressive champions across the country who will join her to make this important push in the next Congress. body:
How could it be this difficult when we did everything right?

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137483426/640932784/-1080040549?refcode=email-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkYWI4YmQ4NS01OTliLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=O_qsuLAKGDHteGV6g6e000ngCl4W1bC3UjX6Tx5EnZc=) I am proud to represent Oregon’s 6th Congressional District and fight for the best interests of Oregonians in Congress. [**Change can happen in a generation. I know because it happened for me.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137483427/640932785/-647546023?refcode=email_081826_bio-survey&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkYWI4YmQ4NS01OTliLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=O_qsuLAKGDHteGV6g6e000ngCl4W1bC3UjX6Tx5EnZc=&emci=246b8ac2-cd94-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=dab8bd85-599b-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=5643047) My dad immigrated from Mexico as a child and worked the fields of the Rio Grande Valley. He dreamed that one day he would work his way out of poverty and make it to the middle class – and went on to do just that. I grew up believing that if we worked hard, anything was possible. But when I got to college, I realized my parents didn’t have the money to pay for my tuition and their groceries. I worked odd jobs to put myself through school. It took seven years, but I finished my degree and became the first person in my family to graduate from college. That got me thinking: [**How could it be this difficult when we did everything right?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137483428/640932786/-647546023?refcode=email_081826_bio-survey&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkYWI4YmQ4NS01OTliLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=O_qsuLAKGDHteGV6g6e000ngCl4W1bC3UjX6Tx5EnZc=&emci=246b8ac2-cd94-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=dab8bd85-599b-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=5643047) I know that’s a question for most families today across Oregon and our nation — that’s why I’m reaching out to you personally. I’m working every day to deliver progress for Oregon — because we deserve leaders who will make life better for all of us. But, change starts with listening. With less than three months until the midterm elections, your voice matters now more than ever before. That’s why I’m reaching out to you today. [**As we approach the primary and the midterms, I need to hear from you about what issues are most important to you, and how you’d like to be involved in the fight to protect our values. Will you take a second to fill out our short survey? Your input has never been more important →**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137483429/640932787/-647546023?refcode=email_081826_bio-survey&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkYWI4YmQ4NS01OTliLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=O_qsuLAKGDHteGV6g6e000ngCl4W1bC3UjX6Tx5EnZc=&emci=246b8ac2-cd94-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=dab8bd85-599b-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=5643047) | | [Take the survey →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137483430/640932788/-647546023?refcode=email_081826_bio-survey&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkYWI4YmQ4NS01OTliLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=O_qsuLAKGDHteGV6g6e000ngCl4W1bC3UjX6Tx5EnZc=&emci=246b8ac2-cd94-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=dab8bd85-599b-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=5643047)

https://elfrethformaryland.com/ [https://elfrethformaryland.com/]

Friend,

Far-right extremists are trying to replace nonpartisan public servants with political loyalists.

As the daughter of two civil servants, I know this isn't just an abstract policy debate. It is a direct attack on the people who keep our country running.

Sitting right on Washington’s doorstep, MD-03 is home to over 45,000 federal workers. That makes our community ground zero for this fight.

I introduced the bipartisan Protect Our Probationary Employees Act to stop illegal worker purges, and I am fighting every day to defend our national institutions. It was the first bipartisan legislative response to the extreme weaponization of DOGE in all of Congress. But holding the line against extreme overreach takes grassroots power.

Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth broke barriers in 2024, becoming the youngest woman ever elected to Congress from Maryland. body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP62/1/120031/images/eon%20header.png]
I need to tell you something I don't talk about enough.
Outside of my office, a group of extremists gathered and screamed what translates to "Death to Krishnamoorthi" at the top of their lungs.
A crowd of people, in America, calling for my death.
I'm an immigrant. The son of people who came to this country with nothing because they believed it was a place where you could live freely, speak freely, and serve your community without fearing for your life. A place where disagreement didn't end in threats of violence.
Sadly, this is nothing new. I have faced this before.
A sitting Republican elected official also publicly tagged the Department of Homeland Security on social media to report me as a "foreign occupier" with an "unpronounceable name" and called for the mass deportation of Indians. I have been mocked, threatened, and told in a hundred different ways that someone like me doesn't belong in American public life.
And every single time, I have made the same choice.
Keep going.
Because the moment I stop — the moment I let the hatred win — is the moment I break faith with every family that came to this country believing it was worth fighting for. Including my own.
This is the America we are living in right now. Extremists feel emboldened to threaten, intimidate, and silence the people who are trying to do the work. Hatred has been given permission to operate in the open. The machinery of government is being used to make certain communities feel like they don't belong.
Equal Opportunity Now exists because we need leaders who have faced this kind of hatred and didn't flinch. Who know what it costs to keep going and choose to keep going anyway. Who will stand up — not just for themselves, but for every family that is being targeted, threatened, and told they don't belong.
Those leaders are out there. And they need our support right now.
Will you chip in $10, $20, or $50 to Equal Opportunity Now and Resist Reclaim Rebuild today to help us elect leaders who won't be intimidated — no matter what they face? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-eon] [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-eon]
CHIP IN TODAY TO DEFEAT MAGA EXTREMISM! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-eon]
They can scream all they want.
We are not slowing down.
— Raja Krishnamoorthi

body:
My answer was simple. I think we can do better.

| | | | |
---
Peter,
I sat down with Joe Birch at Action News 5 earlier this month, and he asked me why I want to be the congressman for Tennessee's 5th Congressional District.
My answer was simple. I think we can do better.
Better than the policies that have been squeezing Tennessee families at the pump, at the grocery store, and at the doctor's office. Better than Washington, which has treated places like Memphis and rural West Tennessee as afterthoughts. Better than the kind of politics that puts party first and people last.
Every one of the 17 counties in TN-05 deserves respectful, dignified representation. That's not a high bar. But it's one that hasn't been met, and I'm ready to change that.

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: Big Tech wants to buy our democracy
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
AI companies and billion-dollar corporations shouldn’t be able to buy influence in our elections.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260818-6613-footer&t=1&akid=6613%2E420207%2E2E0F2R)
Peter, right now it feels like our democracy belongs to the highest bidder.
Billion-dollar corporations, including some of the largest AI companies in the world, are spending enormous sums to influence our elections and shape the policies that govern all of us.
**They're spending millions to protect their profits, weaken oversight, and stack the deck against working families.**
That's why I'm proud to sponsor the **We The People Amendment** to overturn _Citizens United_ and finally get big money out of politics once and for all.
That’s why I've never accepted a dime from corporate PACs. Because I don't work for billionaires, powerful corporations, or special interests.
That’s why I fight for the working people who sent me to Congress. Because I fight for _all of us._
**But standing up to corporate power isn't easy.**
The corporations pouring money into our political system have virtually unlimited resources, and I’m counting on grassroots supporters like you to help me fight back.
[**If you believe our elections should belong to voters, not corporations, will you chip in $3 today to help me continue this fight?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260818.vrEtZ5&refcode=em20260818-6613&amount=3&t=2&akid=6613%2E420207%2E2E0F2R)

Together, we can build a democracy where every voice matters — not just the wealthiest ones.

Pramila Jayapal

Friend, Last week, a far-right Trump advisor led an anti-Muslim and anti-Palestinian onslaught of harassment that pushed two venues to pull out of our Get Out the Vote rally with progressive Florida candidates. Laura Loomer calls herself a “proud Islamophobe” and has called to deport every Muslim American. **Instead of reporting on her hateful intimidation campaign, many media outlets claimed that I was the reason why these venues cancelled on us.** And **today, Islamophobic racists are marching in my district** **— in the beautifully diverse city of Dearborn, which is home to a vibrant Muslim community.** Families are staying home for their safety.
